A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP2F research, with matching core methods, theoretical results and original experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node and graph classification results, component ablations and hyperparameter experiments, including supplementary results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds alternative-source evaluations, efficiency measurements, representation visualizations and a backbone-controlled comparison.

M1.justification: The dual branches, residual adapters, learned fusion, contrastive and topology-consistent losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Added explanations of the projector, fusion coefficient and negative set do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 and Table 10 extend the standard Cora-pretrained node evaluations to PubMed and Computers as source datasets. These add source-to-target transfer conditions within the retained datasets and classification tasks; no new benchmark collection is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 14 adds a GCN-backed GraphLoRA-S comparator alongside its original GAT-backed version and GP2F. The comparator sets in the retained main experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce a GAT-versus-GCN backbone control, five-shot t-SNE comparisons, and parameter, runtime and memory measurements. Existing splits, training budgets and model dimensions remain unchanged. The newly specified neighbor-sampling details document the existing large-graph experiment rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations and adapter-dimension sweeps, Appendices E.3–E.6 add source-dataset robustness, computational-efficiency analysis, representation-clustering visualizations and a backbone fairness check. These substantially broaden the questions examined about GP2F.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 retains five random seeds, 100 independent samplings per seed, the same seed list, and mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. The new accuracy tables follow that practice without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or increased run counts.

E6.justification: The original main results remain unchanged, but Tables 10–14 and Figure 9 add substantial results. Examples include 55.41 ± 8.73 accuracy for PubMed-pretrained GP2F on Cora, 49.63 ± 10.92 for GCN-backed GraphLoRA-S on Cora, and a reported trainable-parameter ratio of 9.23% relative to full fine-tuning. These are additional conditions and measurements, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same assumptions, MSE derivation, optimal fusion weight, strict-improvement theorem and classification-error bound with their proofs. Appendix G discusses their limitations without modifying the formal results.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain strong LP/FT baselines, complementary-branch fusion with a theoretical justification, and effective cross-domain few-shot classification. Changing 'evaluation error' to 'estimation error' in the first contribution bullet clarifies the existing MSE claim rather than introducing a different contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendices F–G discuss fusion-weight behavior under different domain shifts and concrete failure conditions involving weak transferable knowledge or few-shot overfitting. Appendix E also adds interpretations of source sensitivity, computational tradeoffs, clustering and backbone effects, plus adapter-dimension guidance. This substantially expands the interpretation and qualification of the unchanged method.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GP2F code-access statement and URL, specifies 20 sampled neighbors per layer for the existing two-layer large-graph evaluation, clarifies contrastive negatives, and reports parameter and computational costs. Most implementation information in Appendix C.3 is retained; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked code's availability.

R1.justification: Appendices D.2–D.3 expand a largely descriptive literature account into explicit positioning around objective-specific prompting, single adaptation pathways, GraphControl's pre-training dependence, GraphLoRA's source-data requirement and insufficiently constrained knowledge fusion. Three Zhuo et al. (2024) references are also added.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, updates affiliation and publication information, and adds acknowledgments. Related-work paragraphs are rewritten and Appendix E gains named subsections, but the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–14 and the multi-panel t-SNE Figure 9, substantially expanding the evidence displays. Figure 2 changes the adapted-encoder labeling and visual treatment. Existing supplementary plots are retained and relocated; Table 14 also redisplays existing GAT and GP2F results beside the new GCN comparator.

improvement.justification: The alternative-source tests and backbone control strengthen the empirical support, while resource measurements expose computational tradeoffs and Appendix G makes failure conditions clearer. These provide useful supplementary validation and transparency. They do not resolve the gap between the idealized fusion theorem and practical learned fusion; Appendix F's added account of fusion dynamics remains explanatory rather than a measured analysis.
